summary: This bill voids nondisclosure clauses in any contract that bar victims or third parties from disclosing sexual abuse of a minor, applies retroactively, and preempts contrary state laws.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, budgets, or any allocation of government funds. It focuses exclusively on the enforceability of private contractual clauses.
The bill does not address taxes, tax rates, deductions, credits, or any revenue-related measures.
No provisions in the bill relate to healthcare systems, insurance, public coverage, or market-based healthcare delivery.
The bill has no connection to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No references to immigration policy, border enforcement, visas, or pathways to citizenship appear in the legislation.
The bill does not mention abortion, reproductive rights, or any related access or restrictions.
There are no provisions concerning military funding, defense spending, or armed forces policy.
The legislation contains nothing related to environmental regulations, climate policy, or natural resource protections.
No elements of the bill address welfare programs, food assistance, unemployment benefits, or other social safety net policies.
The bill does not engage with schools, education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.
No provisions relate to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.

The bill directly addresses the enforcement of federal criminal laws prohibiting sexual abuse and trafficking of minors (citing chapter 110 and section 1591 of title 18). It voids NDAs that obstruct reporting to law enforcement, frustrate prosecutions, or impede cooperation with authorities. This engages the criminal justice system by removing private barriers to investigation and prosecution of covered crimes, which constitutes a modest reform that facilitates enforcement rather than altering sentencing or policing tactics themselves.
The bill has no bearing on tariffs, trade agreements, globalization, or protectionist measures.
No fiscal provisions, deficit measures, or debt-related policies are present.
The legislation does not address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights issues.
There are no references to foreign aid, international assistance, or related funding.
The bill contains no provisions on voting access, election integrity, voter ID, or electoral reforms.
No content relates to technology regulation, data privacy, or oversight of tech companies.
The bill does not engage with labor rights, union protections, or employer-employee relations.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination rules.
